feedback: Approved. This candidate changes one geometry field from iteration 3: the outer sensor x positions move from ±0.05 to ±0.07, with the inner sensors at ±0.035 and 0. Controller, sensor_size, sensor y and line_loss are unchanged, so any effect comes from the wider footprint. Iteration 3 (kd 0.4, ki 0.5, base_speed 1.2, kp 1.5, sensors at ±0.05, score 342.03) is the best raced design. Its oval finished 16 of 20 runs with max_error 0.043. Its s-bend and slalom both ended off track with progress 0.28 and 0.19, line_loss_events 0.55 and 1.0, and max_error about 0.062 to 0.064. Iterations 0 to 2 showed max_error fixed near 0.061 to 0.065 across changes to kp, kd, ki and base_speed, so the controller is not the main limit on the tighter tracks. The sensor spread is the cheapest untested lever, and the new value is inside the ±0.08 limit. Because the candidate is valid and a clean single-variable test of the best design, approve it so the race returns per-track telemetry. Read the result in this order. (1) If s-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall and their progress rises above 0.4, keep the wider spread and next test sensor y 0.07 to add steering lead. (2) If line_loss stays at 1 per run on the slalom with the wider array, the loss happens at bend entry, so next test sensor_size 0.016 with the same positions. (3) If oval steering_oscillation rises well above 0.28 or the oval finish rate drops below 0.8, the wider spacing is hurting centring on straights, so return the outer sensors to ±0.06 as a compromise.
requested_changes: If s-bend or slalom line_loss_events fall but max_error stays near 0.06, keep geometry.sensor_positions at ±0.07 and move the sensors forward by setting every y to 0.07, to give earlier steering lead on bend entry.

If slalom line_loss_events stay at 1 per run with the wider array, keep the ±0.07 spread and set geometry.sensor_size to 0.016 with the same positions, since iteration 3 showed the outer sensors losing the tape on sharp bends.
If oval steering_oscillation rises well above 0.28 or the oval finish rate drops below 0.8, reduce the outer sensor x values to ±0.06 as a compromise between bend coverage and straight-line centring.
